rows.basis: CCS revenue = Communications 7,126.4M + Enterprise 2,062.1M = 9,188.5M of 12,390.9M total; ATS is excluded. CCS is the hyperscaler data-center line (800G switches, AI/ML compute), not purely AI. Communications grew 81% on data-center networking and Enterprise fell 19% on an AI/ML compute program transition.

The MD&A states HPS was 29% of 2024 revenue (about $2.8B): 0.29 × 9,646M = 2,797.3M, driven by hyperscaler networking demand. HPS is hyperscaler hardware, not strictly AI. It is narrower than the CCS line used for the other years (CCS = Communications 3,946.7M + Enterprise 2,543.8M = 6,490.5M).

CCS revenue = Communications 2,675.6M + Enterprise 1,965.6M = 4,641.2M of 7,961M total; ATS is excluded. This is a data-center and communications line, not AI-specific. Pre-10-K year, so the figures are not cross-checked against XBRL.
CCS revenue = Communications 2,865M + Enterprise 1,406M = 4,271M of 7,250M total; ATS is excluded. It predates the AI ramp and includes telecom and non-AI enterprise hardware.
The Q4 2024 release calls data-center hardware demand robust and cites new AI program awards, including the second and third 1.6T wins. It gives no AI amount.
The company expects $17.0B of total 2026 revenue as demand for AI-related data-center technologies strengthens. That is the whole company, not the AI part, and no AI split is given.

The MD&A says the total 2025 capex of $201.2M went to expanding the Thailand, U.S. and Malaysia sites and design centers 'in support of our growth in AI/ML and HPS programs'. That is the whole capex justified by AI, with no AI amount split out.
The FY2024 MD&A says intended 2025 capital spending was geared to capacity expansion for AI/ML compute and HPS programs. No amount was given.

Total 2026 capex is planned at about $1B (about 6% of revenue) to support growth in customer demand, which the release ties to AI data-center investment. This is the company total, and no AI share is stated.
The MD&A plans higher-than-historical capex in 2027 to support growth in customer demand. No amount and no AI split are given.
The release refers to proprietary R&D investments in AI/ML servers, 1.6T switches and liquid cooling. No amount or share of opex is given.
